Meeting Title: Quarterly product roadmap review
Meeting Date: 2026-10-27

Harper Scott: Harper Scott: Let's anchor the discussion on scope and expected outcome. What has actually changed since the last check-in?
Elijah Davis: Elijah Davis: The current picture is the team has customer evidence for reporting improvements but incomplete sizing for automation. We have nine of fourteen interviewees asked for clearer ownership and export history, and the signal I am watching is the roadmap has capacity for two major bets and one maintenance investment.
Mia Thompson: Mia Thompson: My concern is a broad automation promise could outpace the team's ability to support edge cases. If design research must validate the reporting concepts with administrators, what do we tell the people relying on this work?
Victor Alvarez: Victor Alvarez: We can test a narrow workflow with explicit review before committing to automation breadth. We should keep whether automation should begin with reminders or with task creation visible until that check is complete.
Harper Scott: Harper Scott: For the record, prioritize reporting clarity and a bounded review workflow for the next planning cycle. Elijah Davis will write a one-page outcome brief with success measures and excluded scope before roadmap estimates begin next week; whether automation should begin with reminders or with task creation remains unresolved.
